mainTopic: Redeeming a sold field after two years, selling a field in the יובל year itself, and שמואל's rulings on reversed sales
overview: The משנה teaches that someone who sells his inherited field while the יובל system is in force may not buy it back before two years have passed, based on the פסוק 'במספר שני תבואות'. It explains which years count toward those two years, and רבי אליעזר adds that a buyer may end up eating three crops in two years. The גמרא reads the משנה's words 'not permitted' as a real איסור, so strong that the seller may not even jingle coins to tempt the buyer. Both seller and buyer are bound by an עשה. Next, רב and שמואל argue about a field sold during the יובל year itself. רב says it is sold but goes right back, and שמואל says it is not sold at all. The גמרא defends רב against a קל וחומר and two ברייתות. Finally, רב ענן reports two rulings of שמואל, one about the יובל-year field and one about a slave sold to non-Jews or outside ארץ ישראל. In one of them the sale is reversed and in the other it is not, but he forgot which. רב יוסף proves from a ברייתא that the slave's sale stands, so the field sold in the יובל year is not sold and the money goes back.

steps.title: A sold field cannot be redeemed before two years
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one who sells his field when יובל is in effect may not redeem it for at least two years, learned from 'שני תבואות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who sells his field at a time when the יובל is in effect is not allowed to buy it back less than two years after the sale. The פסוק says, 'According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a basic rule: after selling an ancestral field, the seller must wait at least two years before he can redeem it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'שני', meaning 'years' in the plural, and the smallest plural is two. So the buyer is guaranteed at least two years of crops before the seller can take the field back.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic teaching of the תנאים that the גמרא discusses
The fiftieth year, when sold fields return to their original owners
To redeem, meaning to buy the field back
Years of crops

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sells his field
at a time when the Jubilee is in effect
is not permitted to redeem it
less than two years after the sale,
as it is stated: "According to the number of years of crops
he shall sell to you."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַיּוֹבֵל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sold ancestral field may not be redeemed before two years have passed, based on the plural 'שני' in the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This two-year minimum is the base rule the rest of the משנה and the גמרא build on.

steps.title: Which years count toward the two years
steps.stepSummary: Years of blight, mildew, or שביעית do not count toward the two years. A year in which the buyer plowed the field or left it unused does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the years was a year of blight and mildew, or it was the seventh year, that year does not count toward the total. If the buyer plowed the field or left it unused, that year does count for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how to count the two years. It tells us which years count and which do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of years of crops. So a year in which the land could not produce crops for the buyer (blight, or שביעית) is not counted. If the land could have produced crops and the buyer chose not to use it, that is his own choice, so the year still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Blight, a crop disease caused by a hot wind
Mildew, a disease that turns grain pale
The seventh year, when fields may not be worked
Counts toward the total
He left it unused, without planting

phrases.english: If it was a year of blight and mildew,
or it was the Sabbatical Year —
it does not count toward the tally.
If he plowed it or left it fallow —
it counts for him toward the tally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to count the two years required in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Years when the land cannot produce crops for the buyer do not count. Years the buyer chose not to use do count.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: three crops in two years
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says that if the field was sold before ראש השנה while full of produce, the buyer may eat three crops within the two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: if the owner sold the field to him before ראש השנה while it was full of produce, the buyer eats three crops from it in two years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds a case in which the buyer comes out ahead. He gets three harvests even though only two years pass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer takes the crop that is already standing in the field, and then harvests two more full years. When the seller redeems the field, the buyer does not have to return it full of produce the way he received it.

keyTerms.meaning: The new year, the point from which the years are counted
Full of produce, with crops already standing
Three crops, meaning three harvests

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If he sold it to him before Rosh HaShana
and it was full of produce —
this buyer eats from it
three crops in two years.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a special case about how many harvests fit into the two years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field sold full of produce before ראש השנה can give the buyer three harvests in two years.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: the two-year minimum, which years count, and רבי אליעזר's three-crops case.

steps.title: The wording shows a real prohibition, even against jingling coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the משנה says 'not permitted' rather than 'cannot'. So early redemption is actually forbidden, and the seller may not even tempt the buyer with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said 'One who sells his field when the יובל is in effect' and so on. It does not say 'he cannot redeem'. It says 'he is not permitted to redeem'. This shows the תנא holds that there is also a prohibition, so it is forbidden even to jingle coins in front of the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the exact words of the משנה closely and learns from them that redeeming early is not just ineffective. It is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אינו גואל' would only mean the seller cannot force the buyer to sell back. 'אינו מותר' means it is an איסור. So even persuading the buyer, by jingling money in front of him, is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה by the אמוראים
It does not teach, meaning the משנה did not use these words
Evidently, this shows that
A prohibition
Jingling coins, to tempt someone

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as 'the redemption doesn't work'. The point is stronger: it is forbidden, even with the buyer's agreement.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַיּוֹבֵל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: GEMARA: One who sells his field when the Jubilee is in effect, etc.
It does not teach "he cannot redeem,"
but rather "he is not permitted to redeem."
Evidently he holds that there is also a prohibition,
so that even jingling coins is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Picture the seller rattling money in front of the buyer to tempt him into selling the field back early.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל״ לָא קָתָנֵי, אֶלָּא ״אֵינוֹ מוּתָּר לִגְאוֹל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening line of the משנה and reads its wording closely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Redeeming before two years is an actual איסור, so even tempting the buyer with money is forbidden.

steps.title: Both seller and buyer are commanded by an עשה
steps.stepSummary: The seller is obviously bound by the עשה of 'יִמְכָּר לָךְ'. The גמרא adds that the buyer is also bound by the עשה of 'שָׁנִים תִּקְנֶה', which he would fail to keep by returning the field early.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious for the seller, who is bound by a positive מצוה, as it is written: 'According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.' But even the buyer is bound by a positive מצוה, because we need 'years you shall buy', and that would not happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains who the איסור applies to. Not only the seller, but the buyer too, breaks a positive מצוה if the field goes back before two years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק has two halves. The seller's half is 'he shall sell to you' for years of crops. The buyer's half is 'according to the number of years you shall buy'. If the buyer agrees to an early redemption, he has not bought for 'years', so he fails his own עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say, meaning it is obvious
Is bound by, or stands in violation of, a positive מצוה
The buyer
You shall buy
And it is not there, meaning the requirement is not met

steps.whatToRemember: Early redemption of a sold field is an איסור based on an עשה, and it applies to both sides: the seller ('יִמְכָּר לָךְ') and the buyer ('שָׁנִים תִּקְנֶה').

phrases.english: And it is not necessary to say this about the seller,
who is bound by a positive מצוה, as it is written:
"According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you,"
but even the buyer
is also bound by a positive מצוה,
since we require "years you shall buy," and that is not fulfilled.
phrases.notes: This is the first half of the same פסוק, ויקרא 25:15: 'בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the איסור found in step 4 and shows that it applies to the buyer as well as the seller, each from his own half of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the seller and the buyer are bound by an עשה not to end the sale before two years.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why even the buyer, who might happily take money, may not agree to sell the field back early.

steps.title: Selling a field in the יובל year itself
steps.stepSummary: רב says the field is sold but goes right back to the seller. שמואל says it is not sold at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If someone sells his field during the יובל year itself, רב says it is sold, and it goes out right away. שמואל says it is not sold at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between רב and שמואל about a field sold during the יובל year itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יובל, fields go back to their original owners. רב says the sale still takes effect, but the field leaves the buyer's hands right away. שמואל says the sale never takes hold in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: The fiftieth year, when sold fields go back to their owners
It is sold, and it goes out (back to the seller)
It is not sold at all

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier case. Before, the field was sold while יובל was in effect, in an ordinary year. Here the sale happens during the יובל year itself.

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who sells his field during the Jubilee Year itself,
Rav says: It is sold, and it goes out,
phrases.notes: He means the sale works, but the field goes straight back to the seller.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: and Shmuel says: It is not sold at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a sale made during the יובל year itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the sale takes effect, but the field goes right back. שמואל: the sale does not take effect at all.

steps.title: What is שמואל's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of שמואל's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל holds that the sale does not work at all. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's view is easy to follow: a sale is a sale, and יובל sends the field back. שמואל goes further and says the sale does not happen at all, so the גמרא wants to know his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Shmuel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind שמואל's view in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why a sale made during יובל does not take effect at all.

steps.title: שמואל's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: If a field already sold goes back in יובל, then surely a field not yet sold cannot be sold in יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קל וחומר. A field that was already sold goes back in יובל. So a field that was not yet sold, isn't it logical that it cannot be sold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל learns his view from a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יובל is strong enough to undo a sale that already happened. So it should certainly be strong enough to stop a new sale from taking hold in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Is it not logical? This is the phrase that closes a קל וחומר

phrases.english: An a fortiori inference:
And what, if one that was already sold goes out,
one that is not sold,
is it not logical that it should not be sold?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר, וּמָה מְכוּרָה כְּבָר יוֹצְאָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: יובל undoes a sale that already happened, so it surely blocks a new sale.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב accept this קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses the same kind of קל וחומר: a father cannot sell his daughter once she is a נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב, don't we use a קל וחומר like this? But a ברייתא teaches: I might think a man can sell his daughter when she is a נערה. You can say a קל וחומר: A girl who was already sold goes free now. So a girl who was not sold, isn't it logical that she cannot be sold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. A ברייתא uses the exact same type of קל וחומר that שמואל uses, so why doesn't רב accept it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a girl sold as a maidservant goes free when she becomes a נערה. From this the ברייתא learns that a father cannot sell her once she is a נערה. That is the same shape as שמואל's argument, so the ברייתא seems to support שמואל against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who has reached the first signs of maturity, around age twelve
I might have thought: this sets up a possibility that will be rejected
In this way, like this case

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַב, לָא אָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא?
phrases.english: And according to Rav, do we not say an a fortiori inference in this way?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
One might have thought a person may sell his daughter
when she is a young woman?
You can say an a fortiori inference:
And what, if one already sold now goes out,
one who was not sold,
is it not logical that she cannot be sold?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב, לָא אָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's קל וחומר from step 8 to attack רב's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a sale made during יובל takes effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא accepts the same kind of קל וחומר for a daughter, so רב should accept it for a field too.

steps.title: A daughter is different from a field
steps.stepSummary: A נערה can never be sold again, but a field can be sold again later.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, she cannot be sold again. Here, the field can be sold again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by showing that the daughter case is not like the field case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a girl becomes a נערה, she can never be sold, so it makes sense that no sale works. A field that goes back in יובל can be sold again afterward, so יובל does not cancel the idea of selling it. That is why רב says a sale during יובל does take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here: used to contrast two cases
It can be sold again

steps.whatToRemember: רב holds that the sale works because a field returned in יובל can be sold again later. A נערה can never be sold again, so the ברייתא's קל וחומר does not carry over to a field.

phrases.english: There, she is not sold again;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the daughter who became a נערה.

phrases.english: here, it is sold again.
phrases.notes: Here means the field, which can be sold again after יובל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא הָדְרָא מִיזְדַּבְּנָא, הָכָא הָדְרָא מִיזְדַּבְּנָא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughter's קל וחומר should apply to a field too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A girl can never be sold again, but a field can. So the קל וחומר does not work for a field.

steps.title: A ברייתא about which years a field may be sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a challenge to רב from a ברייתא: 'after the יובל' allows selling close to יובל, and other פסוקים allow selling further from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'Years after the יובל you shall buy.' This teaches that we sell close to the יובל. From where do we learn that we may sell far from the יובל? The פסוק says: 'According to the many years... and according to the few years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to רב by quoting a ברייתא. Here it only sets up the source. The point of the challenge comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the words 'after the יובל' as permission to sell a field in the year close to יובל. From 'many years... few years' it learns that a field may also be sold years away from יובל. The ברייתא speaks of selling after יובל, which seems to be setting up a problem for רב, who allows a sale during יובל itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to the יובל
Far away from the יובל
The פסוק teaches: this brings a source

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"Years after the Jubilee you shall buy":
this teaches that one may sell close to the Jubilee;
from where do we learn one may sell far from the Jubilee?
The verse states:
"According to the many years...
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:16. The price changes with how many years are left, so a sale can happen in any year.

phrases.english: and according to the few years."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב in step 10, the גמרא brings a new challenge to him from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a sale made during the יובל year takes effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא talks about selling after יובל. The full point of the challenge is spelled out in the next lines of the גמרא.

steps.title: The ברייתא says a field sold in the יובל year is not sold
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: in the יובל year itself one may not sell, and if he did, the field is not sold. This seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the יובל year itself a person should not sell his field. And if he did sell it, it is not sold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in step 11. The last line of the ברייתא seems to say a sale in the יובל year does not work at all, which is hard for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a field sold in the יובל year is sold and then goes out. The words 'it is not sold' sound like the sale never happened, which is exactly שמואל's view. So the ברייתא looks like a direct problem for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The 50th year, when fields go back to their original owners
It is not sold

phrases.english: And in the Jubilee Year itself
one may not sell
and if he sold, it is not sold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 11 and delivers the challenge to רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a field sold in the יובל year is sold and then goes out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'it is not sold', which seems to mean the sale does nothing at all.

steps.title: רב: it is sold, just not for the two crop years
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'not sold' means it is not sold for the usual minimum of crop years. It really is sold, and then it goes right back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can say to you: it is not sold for the normal count of crop years. But it is sold, and then it goes out back to the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently. 'Not sold' only means the buyer doesn't get his usual years of crops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a buyer keeps a field for at least two crop years. רב says the ברייתא only takes away those years. The sale itself still happens, but the field leaves the buyer's hands right away.

keyTerms.meaning: The count of crop years the buyer normally gets, at least two
It goes out, meaning it returns to the seller

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
it is not sold for the number of crop years
but it is sold, and it goes out.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not sold' means the sale does nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not sold' means not sold for the crop years. The sale works but the field goes right back.

steps.title: If it is sold, the buyer should get his two years after יובל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the sale works, let the buyer keep the field until after יובל, eat two years of crops, and then return it, just like another ברייתא says.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the field really is sold, let it stay with the buyer until after יובל. After יובל let him eat two years of crops and then give it back! Isn't it taught: if he ate it one year before יובל, they give him another year after יובל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's answer. If the sale is real, why doesn't the buyer get his crop years after יובל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another ברייתא shows that יובל does not cancel the buyer's two-year minimum. If he only got one year before יובל, he gets a second year after it. So if רב says the sale is real, the buyer should get both years after יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: It really is sold
In his possession
They complete for him the missing time

phrases.english: But if it really is sold
let it stand in his possession until after the Jubilee
and after the Jubilee let him eat two years of crops
and then return it!
Isn't it taught:
if he ate it one year before the Jubilee

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ שָׁנָה אַחֶרֶת אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל?
phrases.english: they complete for him another year after the Jubilee?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the field is sold but goes out right away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real sale should earn the buyer his two crop years, even after יובל, as the other ברייתא shows.

steps.title: There he already started eating; here he never did
steps.stepSummary: In the other ברייתא the buyer already entered the field to eat its crops, so he finishes his years. Here he never started, so he gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the buyer already went in to eat from the field. Here, he never went in to eat from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra year after יובל is only for a buyer whose crop years already began before יובל. A field sold in the יובל year itself goes right back, so the buyer never begins eating. That means there is nothing to finish after יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: He went down into the field to eat its crops, meaning his crop years began

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a field sold in the יובל year is sold but goes right back. The buyer gets no crop years because he never began eating from it.

phrases.english: There, he entered to eat
here, he did not enter to eat.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any real sale gives the buyer his crop years, even after יובל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a buyer who already started eating before יובל gets his years finished after it.

steps.title: רב ענן heard two rulings from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן says he heard two things from שמואל: this ruling about selling a field in the יובל year, and that a slave sold to non-Jews or outside ארץ ישראל goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: I heard two things from Master שמואל. One is this one. The other: someone who sells his slave to non-Jews, or outside ארץ ישראל, the slave goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. רב ענן reports two rulings he heard from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling is the one we just learned: שמואל says a field sold in the יובל year is not sold. The second is about an עבד כנעני sold to non-Jews or to someone outside ארץ ישראל: he goes free. רב ענן is setting up a point about both rulings together.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside ארץ ישראל
He goes out to freedom
Two things

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:
I heard two things from Master Shmuel
one is this one
phrases.notes: 'This one' is שמואל's ruling that a field sold in the יובל year is not sold.

phrases.english: and the other: one who sells his slave to non-Jews
or outside the Land
the slave goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links שמואל's ruling about the יובל year to a second ruling of his about selling a slave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל taught two rulings: a field sold in the יובל year is not sold, and a slave sold to non-Jews or outside ארץ ישראל goes free.

steps.title: In one case the sale is cancelled, in the other it isn't, and רב ענן forgot which
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן adds that in one of the two rulings the sale is reversed and the money goes back, and in the other it is not. He does not remember which is which.
steps.simpleTranslation: In one of them the sale is reversed. In the other the sale is not reversed. And I don't know which of them is which.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן finishes his report and admits he forgot one detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings involve a sale that does not fully work. The question is what happens to the money. In one case the sale is cancelled and the money is returned. In the other the sale stays and the buyer loses out. רב ענן cannot remember which case gets which rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The sale is reversed and the money goes back
I don't know

steps.confusionAlert: רב ענן is not unsure whether these rulings exist. He is only unsure which of the two cases gets the money back.

phrases.english: in one, the sale is reversed
and in one, the sale is not reversed
and I do not know which of them.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, meaning 'of them'.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא הָדְרִי זְבִינֵי וַחֲדָא לָא הָדְרִי זְבִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב ענן's report from step 16 and raises the question of which case is which. Steps 18-19 answer it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In one of שמואל's two rulings the sale is reversed, and in the other it is not, but רב ענן forgot which.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא about a slave sold outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tries to solve רב ענן's doubt by quoting a ברייתא: a slave sold outside ארץ ישראל goes free, but still needs a גט שחרור from his second master.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Let us see if we can figure it out from a ברייתא. It teaches that if someone sells his slave outside ארץ ישראל, the slave goes free, but he still needs a document of freedom from his second master.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a source that may solve רב ענן's doubt from Step 17. Here he only quotes the ברייתא. The proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with שמואל that the slave goes free. It also adds a detail: the slave needs a גט שחרור from the 'second master,' meaning the buyer. That small detail is what רב יוסף will build his proof on.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see, an opening for trying to solve a question
A document that frees a slave
His second master, the buyer

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Let us see,
from what is taught in a baraita:
One who sells his slave outside the Land
phrases.notes: The buyer here is a Jew; the problem is only that the slave is taken out of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: the slave goes out to freedom,
but he needs a document of freedom from his second master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt רב ענן raised in Step 17 by bringing an outside source.
steps.raayaObject: Which of שמואל's two rulings reverses the sale and returns the money
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a slave sold outside ארץ ישראל goes free but needs a גט שחרור from his second master

steps.title: The slave's sale stands, so the field's sale is reversed and the money goes back
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא calls the buyer 'his master,' the slave's sale really took effect. So in שמואל's ruling about the field in the יובל year, the sale is undone and the money goes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: since the ברייתא calls the second owner 'his master,' the sale is clearly not reversed. So when שמואל says here that the field is not sold, he means it is not sold and the money goes back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף draws his proof from the wording of the ברייתא. He uses it to decide which of שמואל's two rulings returns the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only someone who really owns the slave can be called 'his master.' So the slave's sale counted, and the buyer loses his money when the slave goes free. רב ענן remembered that in one ruling the money goes back and in the other it does not. Since the slave case is the one where it does not, the field in the יובל year must be the one where the sale is undone and the money is returned.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, a phrase for drawing a conclusion
The sale does not go back, it stays in effect
The money goes back to the buyer

steps.whatToRemember: Slave sold outside ארץ ישראל: the sale stands and he needs a גט שחרור from the buyer. Field sold in the יובל year: the sale is undone and the money goes back.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though the slave goes free, the ברייתא still treats the buyer as his real owner. Going free does not mean the sale never happened.

phrases.english: Learn from it:
since it calls the second one "his master,"
evidently the sale is not reversed,
and when Shmuel says here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means שמואל's ruling about a field sold in the יובל year, from Steps 6-8.

phrases.english: it is not sold, and the money goes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, מִדְּקָרֵי לֵיהּ לְשֵׁנִי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the ברייתא quoted in Step 18 and applies it to רב ענן's doubt.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the slave case the sale is not reversed. In the case of the field sold in the יובל year, the sale is undone and the money goes back to the buyer.
